note: User target was within-1 >= 0.70. Achieved 0.806 (80.6%) within-1 / 0.562 (56.2%) exact on testB chain via a 3-epoch smoke run that completed cleanly. Subsequent 25-epoch full-train attempts produced MPS-side training divergence (loss = 4.8e31, weights exploded) despite grad clipping, NaN guard, deterministic seed, and reduced learning rates. The 3-epoch smoke checkpoint is the deliverable: body_vision_encoder_smoke.pt + body_vision_encoder_smoke_results.json (and a copy promoted to body_vision_encoder.pt for the live API).

phases.name: full_attempts
phases.reason: MPS-side training divergence — loss spiked to 1e31+ within first epoch despite grad clipping at max_norm=1.0 and lr 5e-5/5e-4. Investigated: masks all valid (4.5-8KB), forward pass on initial weights produces sane outputs (-0.06 to 0.05), but training divergence persists across 3 retry attempts with different seeds and hyperparameters. Likely an MPS-specific backward-pass instability with ResNet50 + small batch. Not worth burning more compute given the 3-epoch smoke already exceeded the user target by 10+ pp.

next_actions_for_morning: Result is publishable as-is at the 80.6% within-1 / 56.2% exact bar.
To push higher, the divergence needs root-cause analysis: instrument batch-level loss + grad-norm, try CUDA (Colab) instead of MPS, or use ViT-B/16 backbone which may behave differently under MPS.

For paper text, frame as: "Photo-to-measurement vision encoder trained on BodyM (3 epochs, ResNet50, Apple Silicon MPS) chained to ModCloth-trained size GBM achieves 80.6% within-1 size accuracy from camera + height alone — comfortably above the 70% target the user set, well above the 60.2% h-only baseline."
